Convert a topic model to a data frame

Source: R/accessors.R
as.data.frame.sbert_topic_model.Rd

as.data.frame() returns one of the tables of a fitted topic model as a base data frame. The default, what = "documents", gives one row per modeled unit with its topic, so that the topic of every document (or segment) can be joined to other data, filtered with subset(), or tabulated.

The other tables are the topic sizes ("topics"), the stored terms ("terms"), and the stored representative units ("representatives"), as kept when the model was fitted. To compute terms under other settings, use terms(); to rank representatives in another way, use representatives().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sbert_topic_model'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("documents", "topics", "terms", "representatives")
)

Arguments

x

A topic model fitted by topics().

row.names, optional

Ignored; present for compatibility with the generic.

...

Ignored.

what

Which table: "documents" (default), "topics", "terms", or "representatives".

Value

A base data frame:

  • "documents": one row per modeled unit, with document_id, document_name, segment (segmented fits only), text, topic, label, distance (cosine distance to the topic center), and the columns carried from a data frame input.

  • "topics": one row per topic, with topic, label, n_documents, proportion, and withinss (within-topic sum of squares).

  • "terms": one row per topic and term, with topic, label, term, rank, score, and frequency.

  • "representatives": one row per topic and representative unit, with topic, label, rank, document_id, document_name, segment (segmented fits only), text, and distance.

See also

topic_sizes(), terms(), representatives(), predict().

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
topic_model <- topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
                      embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
head(as.data.frame(topic_model))
